system_description.narrative_title: US–China high‑tech competition: AI, chips and supply‑chain statecraft
system_description.narrative_summary: News cluster centers on an accelerating strategic competition driven by AI demand and semiconductor capacity needs, where government policy (tariffs, export bans, direct financing) and private capital (Nvidia deals, mega‑investments, chip M&A) interact to reshape supply chains for chips, critical minerals and green tech. Markets and corporates are reallocating capital — building fabs, raising financing, and pivoting suppliers — while export controls and trade measures seek to onshore or block key inputs, producing feedbacks across investment, production and geopolitics. The system is open: policies, market confidence, and technology breakthroughs continuously exchange flows with global trade, corporate strategy and national security objectives.
system_description.scope: The ecosystem of AI and semiconductor value chains plus immediate policy and market responses: firms (chipmakers, cloud/data‑center builders, AI vendors), capital flows and financing deals, mineral and battery supply chains, export controls/tariffs and industrial subsidies, and short‑term market sentiment and stock moves.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical‑economic order shaped by US–China strategic rivalry and the evolution of technology‑led globalization
adjacent_subsystems: Global capital markets and investor sentiment (equities, financing vehicles)
Critical minerals and battery supply chains (mining, processing, export controls)
Trade, export controls and industrial policy (tariffs, subsidies, security reviews)
Corporate tech manufacturing and data‑center infrastructure (fabs, power, chip startups)

variables.name: AI compute demand
variables.description: The aggregate demand for high‑performance compute resources to train and run advanced AI models.

variables.name: Semiconductor production capacity
variables.description: The installed wafer fab and packaging capacity available to manufacture integrated circuits across the ecosystem.

variables.name: Fab construction rate
variables.description: The pace at which new fabrication and assembly facilities are initiated and built per unit time.

variables.name: Export control intensity
variables.description: The degree and strictness of restrictions on cross‑border transfers of technologies, inputs and equipment.

variables.name: Industrial subsidy level
variables.description: The magnitude of direct public financial support, tax incentives and price guarantees for targeted industrial activities.

variables.name: Private investment flow
variables.description: Net capital deployed by private sources into production, R&D and infrastructure in the technology and manufacturing chain per unit time.

variables.name: Supply‑chain diversification
variables.description: The geographic and supplier dispersion of inputs and intermediate goods across the value chain.

variables.name: Critical minerals availability
variables.description: The accessible physical stock and near‑term producible quantity of minerals and materials essential to chip, battery and green technologies.

variables.name: Technology breakthrough rate
variables.description: The frequency and magnitude of novel technical advances that materially change performance, cost or capability in computing and materials.

variables.name: Trade barrier level for chips
variables.description: The cumulative tariff, quota and non‑tariff impediments applied specifically to semiconductor goods and related inputs.

variables.name: Onshoring share of production
variables.description: The proportion of critical manufacturing and assembly activities located within a jurisdictional area relative to global output.

variables.name: Financing costs
variables.description: The effective cost and availability of capital for large‑scale industrial and infrastructure projects in the sector.

variables.name: Market confidence in tech
variables.description: The aggregated investor and buyer expectations about future profitability and risk of technology‑driven firms and assets.

variables.name: Skilled talent supply
variables.description: The stock of trained engineers, researchers and technicians available to design, build and operate advanced semiconductor and AI systems.

variables.name: Strategic security priority
variables.description: The emphasis placed by policy frameworks on securing supply chains and technology for national security objectives.

variables.name: Trade flow volatility
variables.description: The short‑term variability in cross‑border shipments of components, finished goods and critical inputs.

catalysts.title: Nvidia–Wall Street $500bn AI financing push
catalysts.description: A large financing vehicle led by Nvidia and asset managers to fund AI infrastructure and projects, mobilising private capital into the sector.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Nvidia, Wall Street Firms Strike AI Financing Deal Targeting $500 Billion" (2026-08-10).

catalysts.title: SK Hynix $38bn memory-plant expansion
catalysts.description: SK Hynix's board-approved $38 billion plan to build new memory fabs, increasing global memory production capacity over coming years.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "SK Hynix to invest $38 billion building new memory chip plants" (2026-08-08).

catalysts.title: SpaceX/Tesla Terafab chip plant in Texas
catalysts.description: Planned Terafab investment in Texas to produce chips at scale for AI/cloud customers, initiating large U.S. fabrication activity.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "SpaceX, Tesla to initially spend $16.8 billion on Terafab chip plant in Texas" (2026-08-08).

catalysts.title: U.S. tariffs and minimum prices on solar and components
catalysts.description: Administration plans to impose a 15% tariff and minimum prices on solar panels/components; broader trade actions aim to compete with China on clean tech and chips.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Trump to Impose 15% Tariff, Set Minimum Prices on Solar Panels and Components" and "Trump unveils trade actions to compete with China on solar and chips" (2026-08-08/09).

catalysts.title: U.S. mineral financing and pledges
catalysts.description: Multiple U.S. commitments (~$3bn plus additional grants/awards) to domestic and allied minerals projects to strengthen defense and battery supply chains.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Trump administration to invest $3 billion into minerals projects" and "U.S. Pledges $2 Billion for Battery, Materials Producers" (2026-08-08/10).

catalysts.title: DR Congo ban on copper and cobalt concentrate exports
catalysts.description: Congo's export ban/order on concentrates limits primary flows of copper/cobalt, disrupting global upstream supplies and refining chains.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "EXCLUSIVE: Congo bans copper and cobalt concentrates exports" (2026-08-08/09).

catalysts.title: Nvidia investments in Lancium / datacenter capacity
catalysts.description: Nvidia's reported multibillion-dollar investments in Lancium/Stargate-style data-center and power projects to expand AI compute capacity.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Nvidia to invest up to $3 billion in Lancium" and related datacenter investment stories (2026-08-08/09/10).

catalysts.title: Political push to block advanced chips to sanctioned Chinese firms
catalysts.description: Lawmakers and regulators pressing to stop advanced semiconductors reaching sanctioned Chinese firms, likely prompting tighter export rules and enforcement.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Key Republican urges US to stop any advanced chips from reaching sanctioned Chinese firms" (2026-08-10).

catalysts.title: China's 'Ice Silk Road' Arctic shipping expansion
catalysts.description: Beijing's use of Arctic routes to bypass traditional chokepoints, changing freight patterns and alternative logistics for goods and inputs.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "China bypasses shipping chokepoints with ‘Ice Silk Road’ through Arctic" (2026-08-10).

catalysts.title: Sony–TSMC $6.3bn image-sensor joint build
catalysts.description: Planned $6.3 billion joint investment to co-manufacture image sensors, expanding capacity in a specific semiconductor niche.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Sony, TSMC to spend $6.3 billion to jointly make image sensors" (2026-08-10).

catalysts.title: Apple testing CXMT memory chips
catalysts.description: Apple trials memory chips from China's CXMT to ease AI-driven supply crunch, potentially shifting sourcing and procurement decisions.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Apple tests memory chips from China’s CXMT to ease AI-driven supply crunch" (2026-08-09).
